title: The Emerging Generative Artificial Intelligence Divide in the United States
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether awareness of generative AI is unevenly distributed across the United States in ways that resemble older digital divides. Rather than studying classroom use or instructional effects, it asks where interest in ChatGPT was concentrated during the first six months after its public release and what county-level demographic, socioeconomic, and industry factors were associated with that awareness.

The study uses de-identified Bing search logs from December 1, 2022 to May 31, 2023, aggregated to ZIP code and county level, and combines them with American Community Survey data. The authors map spatial clustering of ChatGPT search interest, test for hotspots and coldspots, and fit multilevel negative binomial regression models with state random effects. The population is U.S. residents at the county level, with analysis focused on adult search behavior rather than any education-specific subgroup.

The main finding is that early ChatGPT awareness was concentrated in more urban, educated, and economically advantaged counties, especially along the West Coast and in major metropolitan areas, while coldspots appeared in the Gulf South, Appalachia, and parts of the Midwest. Educational attainment was the strongest predictor and substantially attenuated other associations in adjusted models. The paper concludes that generative AI adoption is already reflecting existing socioeconomic and spatial inequalities, raising concerns that the technology could reinforce rather than reduce disparities without targeted intervention.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s conversational generative AI chatbot built on a GPT-family large language model.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the focal technology for measuring awareness/adoption via Bing search interest in the first six months after its public release; the paper does not evaluate instructional use or educational outcomes.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a correlational, observational study using search-log and county-level census data, not an intervention or causal evaluation of AI use in education. It provides descriptive evidence about awareness patterns rather than experimental evidence of effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports sizable geographic and socioeconomic disparities in awareness of ChatGPT, but it does not test learning, coaching, or classroom outcomes. Its impact is therefore indirect and primarily about adoption patterns rather than demonstrated educational effect.
